What is Sabai grass?

Sabai grass is a perennial grass that grows in eastern and central India, especially Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. It grows naturally in dry forest areas, needs very little water and almost no chemical inputs, which makes it a sustainable craft fibre. Its long, tough blades are twisted into rope or coiled and stitched into baskets and other products.

Benefits of Sabai grass

  • Durable: strong natural fibres that last for years in daily use.
  • Biodegradable and plastic-free: Sabai products break down naturally at the end of their life.
  • Low water use: the grass grows with minimal irrigation.
  • Craft-friendly: it can be dyed, twisted, coiled or braided, so artisans can make many shapes and colours.
  • Good for land: its roots help bind soil.

What is made from Sabai grass?

  • Home décor: wall plates, trays, vases, lampshades
  • Storage: baskets, boxes and organisers
  • Bags: totes and handbags
  • Planters: grass planters and pot covers
  • Tableware: placemats, coasters, roti and fruit baskets
  • Gifting: reusable hamper baskets and gift boxes

The artisans behind Sabai craft

In districts such as Mayurbhanj (Odisha) and Purulia (West Bengal), Sabai weaving is an important livelihood, much of it done by women working from home, often organised through self-help groups. GrassCrafts works with these artisans to bring their work to buyers across India.

How to care for Sabai grass products

Dust or wipe with a dry cloth. Keep away from long exposure to water and harsh sun; if a piece gets wet, dry it in shade. Store in a dry, airy place.

FAQ

What is Sabai grass called in English?

Its botanical name is Eulaliopsis binata. In English it is usually just called Sabai grass; it is known as Sabai ghas in Odisha and Babui ghas in Bengal.

Where does Sabai grass grow in India?

Mainly in Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, in dry forest areas.

What are Sabai grass products used for?

Storage baskets, gift boxes, bags, wall décor, planters, trays and table mats – all plastic-free and biodegradable.

By Sristi Dey, founder, GrassCrafts

Sabai grass (Eulaliopsis binata) is called Sabai ghas in Odisha and Babui ghas in Bengal. It grows in the dry forest areas of Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh and needs very little water. Artisans twist the blades into rope or coil and stitch them into shapes. Which Sabai grass product should you buy?

For storage at home

Choose a basket with a frame or a lid if you want it to hold its shape. The kitchen basket suits fruit and vegetables, the lidded basket hides clutter, and the floor basket works for bulkier items. More options are in our storage baskets.

For gifting

Boxes with lids make the most useful gifts because the recipient keeps them for jewellery, dry fruit or puja items. The round gift boxes come in several colours and the gift box is the lowest-priced option. For hampers, see the wedding gift hampers and corporate gifts.

For plants

The Sabai grass planters are meant as pot covers and basket planters. Keep the plant in its own plastic or ceramic pot inside, so water never touches the weave.

For the table and the wall

Round table mats and wall plates are the easiest way to add a handwoven look to a room without taking up space. Wall plates come in 10 designs and in sets.

For the office and for carrying

How do you choose a good Sabai grass product?

  • Look at the weave. Tight, even coils with firm stitching are a good sign. Loose ends should be tucked in.
  • Match the shape to the job. Frames and lids keep their shape; open baskets are better for light items.
  • Expect small variations. Each piece is handmade, so size and colour can differ slightly from the photo.
  • Check the size on the product page before you order, especially for planters and boxes.

How is a Sabai grass product made?

The long blades are dried, then twisted into a rope or coiled by hand. The coils are stitched round and round into the shape of a basket, box, tray or plate, and the fibre can be dyed so artisans can make many colours. Because every coil is placed by hand, a piece can take real time to finish, and no two are exactly alike. In districts such as Mayurbhanj in Odisha and Purulia in West Bengal, Sabai weaving is an important livelihood, much of it done by women working from home, often organised through self-help groups.

Prices are the lowest variant price on each product page and can change, so confirm the current price before you order. Orders above ₹1,250 ship free across India, so combining a planter, a table mat and a box often gets you past that mark.

How do you care for Sabai grass?

Dust or wipe with a dry cloth. Keep it away from long exposure to water and harsh sun; if a piece gets wet, dry it in shade. Store it in a dry, airy place.

Why choose Sabai grass over plastic or other fibres?

Sabai grass is strong, biodegradable and plastic-free. It grows with minimal irrigation and its roots help bind soil. If you are still deciding, our jute, water hyacinth, Sabai and cane comparison sets them side by side.

Storage baskets, gift boxes, bags, wall décor, planters, trays and table mats. All are plastic-free and biodegradable.

Yes. Water hyacinth is an invasive aquatic plant — harvesting it for craft actually helps restore local ecosystems. Our baskets divert approximately 850g of plant matter that would otherwise choke waterways, while saving an estimated 2,400 litres of water compared to conventional materials.
